hero.headline:
Stop losing money
on APIs you don't
even remember using
hero.description: Custe.AI centralizes all your spend on third-party APIs in a single dashboard — with automatic alerts, history, and cost projections.

problem.title: Your API spend is everywhere
problem.subtitle: Small and mid-size businesses spend hours every month trying to understand what they consumed — and often find out too late.

card1.title: Centralized dashboard
card1.content: Track spend across providers in real time with clear charts, smart KPIs, and a consolidated view of your operation.

card2.title: Smart alerts
card2.content: Set spend limits and get notified automatically when consumption reaches critical levels. No more discovering a budget overrun at invoice time.

card3.title: History & trends
card3.content: Analyze how costs evolve by day, week, or month and spot unexpected increases, waste, and seasonality.

card4.title: Provider comparison
card4.content: Quickly find out which provider delivers the best value for your company and make decisions based on real data.

card5.title: API management
card5.content: Centralize keys, providers, limits, and settings in a single secure, organized environment.

solution.title: One dashboard to govern all your costs
solution.subtitle: Custe.AI brings real financial clarity to anyone using third-party APIs.

feature1.title: Centralized registration
feature1.desc: Add all your APIs in one place — name, provider, access key, currency, and monthly limit. Everything encrypted.

feature2.title: CSV upload
feature2.desc: Upload invoices from any provider. The system normalizes and matches the records automatically.

feature3.title: Real-time charts
feature3.desc: Pie and line charts, growth KPIs, and projections — all updated after each upload.

feature4.title: Automatic alerts
feature4.desc: Set thresholds per API (e.g. 80% of the limit). When reached, you get an in-app and email notification — before you blow the budget.

feature5.title: Role-based access
feature5.desc: Admin, Analyst, and Developer — each role sees only what it needs, with granular permissions.

feature6.title: Provider comparison
feature6.desc: Compare similar API costs side by side, like AWS vs Azure, and make decisions grounded in real data.

plans.title: Transparent as it should be
plans.subtitle: No surprises. Exactly what you expect from a cost-control tool.

guide.title: User Guide
guide.subtitle: Everything you need to know to get the most out of API Cost Shield — step by step.
guide.tipText: Start by creating a provider, then enable automatic polling or send your first webhook. Within minutes you'll see real cost data on your Dashboard.
guide.footerNote: Need more help? Check the Changelog for the latest features or reach out to your workspace admin.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.subtitle: Register your account, create a workspace, and sign in for the first time.

step1.title: Create an account
step1.desc: Visit the Register page, enter your email, a strong password (min. 8 chars, with a number and special character), a display name, workspace name, timezone, and base currency. The first user of a workspace automatically becomes admin.

step2.title: Sign in
step2.desc: Use your email and password on the Sign In page. Your session is stored in a secure httpOnly cookie — no tokens are exposed to JavaScript.

step3.title: Explore the sidebar
step3.desc: The left sidebar gives you access to Dashboard, Providers, Cost Allocation, Settings, Users (admins only), Changelog, and this User Guide.

step4.title: Add your first provider
step4.desc: Go to Providers → Add provider. Fill in the name, provider type, and billing type. Your API key is encrypted before being stored on the server.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Monitor your total API spend, growth trends, and per-provider breakdowns in real time.

step1.title: Read the summary cards
step1.desc: The four cards at the top show: current month total, previous month total, growth percentage vs last month, and your workspace's base currency.

step2.title: Filter by month
step2.desc: Type a month in yyyy-mm format (e.g. 2025-06) in the Month field to inspect historical data. Leave blank for the current month.

step3.title: Filter by tag
step3.desc: Enter a Tag Key (e.g. 'team') and Tag Value (e.g. 'ml-ops') to scope all cards and charts to a specific dimension.

step4.title: Group pie chart by tag
step4.desc: Type a tag key in 'Group pie by tag' to switch the pie chart from provider-based to tag-value-based slices — perfect for comparing team spend.

step5.title: Read the projection card
step5.desc: When available, the Projection card shows a linear end-of-month spend estimate based on your current daily run rate. Use it for early budget warnings.

providers.title: Providers
providers.subtitle: Register and manage the AI / API services whose costs you want to track.

step1.title: Add a provider
step1.desc: Click 'Add provider', enter a display name, choose the provider kind (e.g. openai, aws, stripe, generic), set billing type (postpaid or prepaid), and optionally add a health-check URL.

step2.title: Enter your API key
step2.desc: Paste your provider API key in the Access Key field. It is encrypted with Fernet before being stored — treat it like a password and never share it.

step3.title: Set a monthly budget
step3.desc: In the Budgets tab, enter a Monthly Limit in your base currency. Alerts fire automatically at 80% and 100% of the budget.

step4.title: Run the health probe
step4.desc: Use the Health tab to ping your provider's health URL on demand and confirm it is reachable.

step5.title: View invoices
step5.desc: The Invoices tab lets you register invoice snapshots (period start/end, notes, object key). These act as a permanent audit trail of your billing history.

step6.title: Delete or archive
step6.desc: Providers can be updated at any time. Credentials, polling config, tags, and budget limits each have their own tab for focused editing.

polling.title: Automatic Polling
polling.subtitle: Let the platform fetch costs from your provider APIs automatically — no webhooks required.

step1.title: Enable polling
step1.desc: Go to Providers → select a provider → Polling tab. Toggle 'Enable automatic polling'. Currently supported: OpenAI (usage API). More adapters are in progress.

step2.title: Set the interval
step2.desc: Enter a polling interval in seconds (minimum 300 s / 5 min). Leave blank to use the global default. The platform will fetch costs on that schedule.

step3.title: Test the connection
step3.desc: Click 'Test Connection' to validate that your API key can reach the provider. A green success message confirms credentials are valid.

step4.title: Monitor polling health
step4.desc: The Polling Status section shows the last polled timestamp, consecutive failures, and next retry time. On first poll, 30 days of historical data are backfilled automatically.

webhooks.title: Webhooks & Integration
webhooks.subtitle: Push cost events from Stripe or any HMAC-signed gateway directly into the platform.

step1.title: Find your webhook URLs
step1.desc: Go to Providers → select a provider → Integration tab. You'll see a Stripe webhook URL and a Generic HMAC webhook URL. Copy the relevant one.

step2.title: Configure on the provider side
step2.desc: Paste the URL into your Stripe Dashboard (or gateway) as a webhook endpoint. Set the webhook secret to match the one stored in the platform.

step3.title: Verify with curl
step3.desc: The Integration tab provides a ready-made curl example for the generic HMAC endpoint and Stripe CLI command. Use them to send a test event and confirm ingestion.

manualCosts.title: Manual Cost Entry
manualCosts.subtitle: Record one-off or corrective cost lines directly from the UI without a webhook.

step1.title: Open the manual form
step1.desc: Go to Providers → select a provider → scroll to the 'Manual cost line' section below the provider details.

step2.title: Fill in the cost
step2.desc: Enter the amount in the original currency, the ISO currency code (e.g. USD), and optionally a tags JSON object (e.g. {"team": "ml-ops"}).

step3.title: Record the cost
step3.desc: Click 'Record cost'. The event is immediately ingested and will appear in your Dashboard on the next data refresh.

costAllocation.title: Cost Allocation
costAllocation.subtitle: Cross-tabulate spend by tag dimensions across all providers to understand who is spending what.

step1.title: Navigate to Cost Allocation
step1.desc: Click 'Cost Allocation' in the sidebar. This page lets you slice spend across multiple tag keys at once.

step2.title: Enter tag keys
step2.desc: Type one or more tag keys separated by commas (e.g. 'team,env'). These must match the tag keys you've configured on your providers or cost events.

step3.title: Generate the report
step3.desc: Click 'Generate report' (or press Enter). The table shows each tag-key/tag-value pair as a row, with a spend column per provider and a row total.

step4.title: Read the summary cards
step4.desc: Three summary cards above the table show: Grand Total, number of tag keys analyzed, and total row count. Use the Month field to scope the report to a specific billing period.

tags.title: Tags & Cost Labels
tags.subtitle: Attribute every cost event to a team, project, or environment using a flexible tagging system.

step1.title: Set default tags on a provider
step1.desc: Go to Providers → select a provider → Tags tab. Enter a JSON object like {"team": "ml-ops", "env": "prod"}. All cost events from this provider will inherit these tags automatically.

step2.title: Override tags per event
step2.desc: When recording a manual cost or sending a webhook payload, include a 'tags' field. Event-level values override provider defaults on key conflict.

step3.title: Backfill existing events
step3.desc: Changed your default tags? Click 'Backfill existing events' in the Tags tab to re-apply the updated tags to all historical cost events for that provider. Event-level overrides are preserved.

step4.title: Filter by tags on the Dashboard
step4.desc: Use the Tag Key and Tag Value filters on the Dashboard to scope all metrics and charts to a specific dimension (e.g. team=frontend).

budgets.title: Budgets & Alerts
budgets.subtitle: Set monthly spending limits per provider and get notified before you overspend.

step1.title: Set a monthly limit
step1.desc: Go to Providers → select a provider → Budgets tab. Enter a Monthly Limit in your base currency. Zero or empty means no limit.

step2.title: Set a prepaid balance
step2.desc: For prepaid billing models, enter the Prepaid Balance. The platform tracks usage against this balance.

step3.title: Alert thresholds
step3.desc: Alerts fire automatically at 80% and 100% of the monthly limit. The Dashboard projection card will also highlight providers trending over budget.

analytics.title: Analytics & Charts
analytics.subtitle: Visualise spending patterns with pie charts, cumulative spend timelines, and projection models.

step1.title: Pie chart — share by provider
step1.desc: Shows each provider's proportion of total spend for the selected month. Hover slices for exact amounts. Toggle to a tag-based pie by entering a tag key in 'Group pie by tag'.

step2.title: Line chart — cumulative MTD
step2.desc: Shows spend accumulated day by day through the current (or selected) month. A steeper slope means faster spend acceleration.

step3.title: Projection card
step3.desc: A linear regression on daily spend predicts the end-of-month total. The model note describes the confidence level. Use this to intervene early if trajectory exceeds budget.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Configure your workspace name, timezone, base currency, and advanced operations.

step1.title: Update workspace details
step1.desc: In the Workspace section, you can view your active Tenant ID and update workspace-level preferences.

step2.title: Change language
step2.desc: Select your preferred language (English or Portuguese) from the Language dropdown. The change applies immediately across the entire interface.

step3.title: Operations (advanced)
step3.desc: The Ops section is for administrators. Enter the X-Ops-Secret header value to trigger maintenance routes like monthly rollups and alerts scans. The secret is stored in session storage only.

users.title: Users & Invitations
users.subtitle: Manage team members, roles, and pending invitations from the Users page (admin only).

step1.title: Invite a team member
step1.desc: Go to Users → Invite user. Enter the colleague's email and choose a role (Editor or Viewer). Click 'Send invite' to generate a secure 8-character invite code.

step2.title: Share the invite link
step2.desc: After sending, a dialog shows the full invite URL. Share it directly with your colleague. It expires in 48 hours and can only be redeemed once.

step3.title: Manage pending invites
step3.desc: The Pending Invitations table lists all open invites with expiry times. Copy the link again or click Revoke to cancel an invite before it is used.

step4.title: Understand roles
step4.desc: admin: full access including user management. editor: can create/update providers and record costs. viewer: read-only access to all data. Roles are hierarchical — higher roles inherit all lower-role permissions.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.subtitle: Create multiple workspaces or join an existing one without creating a new account.

step1.title: Create a new workspace
step1.desc: In the sidebar bottom section, click 'Create workspace', enter a workspace name, and confirm. You become the admin of the new workspace automatically.

step2.title: Join via invite code
step2.desc: If you received an invite code (not a full link), paste it in the 'Join workspace' input in the sidebar and click the plus button.

step3.title: Switch between workspaces
step3.desc: When you belong to more than one workspace, a dropdown appears in the sidebar. Select any workspace to switch context instantly. Your JWT is re-issued with the new active workspace.

security.title: Security Overview
security.subtitle: How the platform protects your data, credentials, and sessions.

step1.title: JWT authentication
step1.desc: Access tokens expire in 15 minutes; refresh tokens expire in 7 days. Both are stored in httpOnly, SameSite=strict cookies — never accessible to JavaScript.

step2.title: Encrypted credentials
step2.desc: All API keys and webhook secrets are encrypted with Fernet (AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256) before being written to the database. They are only decrypted in memory at runtime.

step3.title: HMAC webhook verification
step3.desc: Incoming webhook payloads are verified using HMAC-SHA256 against the stored webhook secret. Tampered or unsigned payloads are rejected automatically.

credentials.title: Updating Credentials
credentials.subtitle: Rotate API keys and webhook secrets for any provider without downtime.

step1.title: Open the Credentials tab
step1.desc: Go to Providers → select a provider → Credentials tab. You'll see fields for the API Key and Webhook Secret.

step2.title: Enter new values
step2.desc: Leave a field blank to keep the current value. Only the fields you fill in will be updated. The new key is encrypted before storage.

step3.title: Save and verify
step3.desc: Click 'Update credentials', then use the Test Connection button in the Polling tab to confirm the new key is valid.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.subtitle: Stay up to date with every new feature, fix, and security improvement.

step1.title: Read the timeline
step1.desc: The Changelog page lists every release in reverse chronological order. Each entry shows the version number, release date, and a list of tagged items.

step2.title: Understand the tags
step2.desc: feature (blue) = new capability. fix (amber) = bug correction. security (green) = security improvement. changed (purple) = modified behaviour. removed (red) = deprecated/removed functionality.
